summary: Monroe County, WV lookout site (US 1679) now under a private owner; observers recorded in 1957 and 1960; firelookout.org lists the tower as gone.

facts.status_note: firelookout.org lists 'Tower Gone'; the register gives no removal date or description
facts.agency: Private owner (formerly West Virginia Division of Forestry)

access.note: Register names a private owner; no source says whether visitors may enter the land

events.note: Item dated October 6, 1957: observers for District 4 chosen to go on duty at the start of hunting season; L.E. Long listed at Brushy Mountain (as quoted on Forest Lookouts)
Item dated October 13, 1960: all District Four towers manned; Ray Collins of Rupert at Brushy Mountain (as quoted on Forest Lookouts)
Registered January 26, 2017 as US 1679, WV 70; nominated by Brian M. Powell

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says Monroe County. The Forest Lookouts page heads its entry Greenbrier/Monroe Counties, and the 1957 observer's address reads Greenbrier. The story uses Monroe, the register's listing.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only history is two newspaper items (1957, 1960) quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. No construction date, removal date, description or photo was found in the pages read or in one web search. The brief's access 'unknown' is changed to private on the strength of the register's private-owner line; please confirm that is the level you want. Brief county Monroe matches the register; the Forest Lookouts header says Greenbrier/Monroe.
